conversations.title: Meeting a neighbour on the stairs
conversations.goal: Greet politely, say who you are, where you are from and what you do.

turns.de: Grüß Gott! Sind Sie neu hier?
turns.en: Hello! Are you new here?

turns.de: Grüß Gott! Ja, ich wohne seit Kurzem hier.
turns.en: Hello! Yes, I've only just moved in.
alt: Guten Morgen! Ja, ich bin neu hier.

turns.de: Willkommen! Ich bin Frau Huber, von Tür vier.
turns.en: Welcome! I'm Mrs Huber, from door four.
Nice to meet you! My name is Danish.

turns.de: Freut mich auch. Woher kommen Sie?
turns.en: Nice to meet you too. Where are you from?

turns.de: Ich komme aus ... und ich studiere hier an der Uni.
turns.en: I'm from ... (your country), and I study at the university here.

turns.de: Ah, schön! Und Sie sprechen schon Deutsch!
turns.en: Oh, nice! And you already speak German!
A little. I'm still learning.

turns.de: Das ist doch schon sehr gut. Einen schönen Tag noch!
turns.en: That's already very good. Have a nice day!
Thanks, same to you! Goodbye!

key_phrases.en: I've only just moved in here.

notes: Use Sie with neighbours you don't know, especially older ones. Wait for them to offer du.
Many Viennese doors are numbered (Tür 4). Neighbours often introduce themselves by surname: Frau Huber, Herr Novak.

conversations.title: When you don't understand
conversations.goal: Stay in German with repair phrases instead of switching to English.

turns.de: Entschuldigung, wissen Sie, wo hier die nächste Trafik ist?
turns.en: Excuse me, do you know where the nearest kiosk is?

turns.de: Entschuldigung, ich lerne noch Deutsch. Können Sie das bitte wiederholen?
turns.en: Sorry, I'm still learning German. Can you repeat that, please?

turns.de: Klar. Die Trafik. Wo ist die nächste Trafik?
turns.en: Sure. The kiosk. Where is the nearest kiosk?
What does Trafik mean?

turns.de: Ein kleines Geschäft. Für Zeitungen und Fahrscheine.
turns.en: A small shop. For newspapers and tickets.

turns.de: Ah, ich verstehe. Ich glaube, da vorne links.
turns.en: Ah, I understand. I think it's up ahead on the left.
Great, thanks!
You're welcome!

notes: Repair phrases count as successful German. Most people slow down happily when you ask.

conversations.title: Sharing a table in the Mensa
conversations.setting: University canteen at lunchtime. The tables are full.
conversations.goal: Ask for a seat, return Mahlzeit, say what you study.

turns.en: Excuse me, is this seat free?
Yes, sure. Sit down!
Thanks! Enjoy your lunch!

turns.de: Mahlzeit! Bist du auch hier an der Uni?
turns.en: Enjoy! Are you at the university here too?
Yes, I study here.
Cool. What do you study?

turns.de: Informatik. Das Studium ist auf Englisch.
turns.en: Computer science. The programme is in English.

turns.de: Und du lernst trotzdem Deutsch? Super!
turns.en: And you're learning German anyway? Great!

turns.de: Ja, ich möchte hier mit Leuten Deutsch sprechen.
turns.en: Yes, I want to speak German with people here.
I'm Paul, by the way.
I'm Danish. Nice to meet you!

key_phrases.de: Ich möchte mit Leuten Deutsch sprechen.
key_phrases.en: I want to speak German with people.

notes: Mahlzeit! is a normal lunchtime greeting in Austrian canteens and offices. Answer with Mahlzeit!
Students say du to each other straight away.

conversations.title: Introducing yourself at a student event
conversations.goal: Keep a first chat going for about a minute.

turns.de: Hallo! Ich bin Anna. Und du?
turns.en: Hi! I'm Anna. And you?
Hi, my name is Danish.
Where are you from, Danish?

turns.de: Aus ... Und du? Bist du aus Wien?
turns.en: From ... (your country). And you? Are you from Vienna?

turns.de: Ja, ich bin eine echte Wienerin. Wie lange bist du schon hier?
turns.en: Yes, I'm a real Viennese. How long have you been here?
For a few months.
And do you like it in Vienna?

turns.de: Ja, sehr! Wien ist schön und sehr sicher.
turns.en: Yes, a lot! Vienna is beautiful and very safe.

turns.de: Was machst du gern in deiner Freizeit?
turns.en: What do you like doing in your free time?

turns.de: Ich koche gern und ich gehe gern spazieren.
turns.en: I like cooking and I like going for walks.

turns.de: Wo gehst du am liebsten spazieren?
turns.en: Where do you like walking most?
Along the Danube Canal or in the Prater.

turns.de: Schön! Wir können ja mal zusammen einen Kaffee trinken.
turns.en: Nice! We could have a coffee together some time.
Yes, I'd like that!

key_phrases.de: Wie lange bist du schon hier?
key_phrases.en: How long have you been here?
Do you like it in Vienna?

notes: Und du? is your best friend: answer, then ask back.
gern + verb = like doing: Ich lese gern, Ich spiele gern Cricket.

conversations.title: At the supermarket checkout
conversations.goal: Handle the three questions every cashier asks.

turns.en: Hello! Do you have a loyalty card?
No, unfortunately not.
Do you need a bag?
Yes, one please.
By card, please.
There you go. Do you need the receipt?
No, thanks.
Have a nice day!
Thanks, same to you! Goodbye!

notes: Austrian supermarkets ask about their own loyalty card (at Billa and Penny it's the jö card). Nein, danke is a fine answer.
Sackerl is the Austrian word for bag.

conversations.title: At the bakery
conversations.setting: A small bakery in the morning. There is a queue.
conversations.goal: Order bread rolls and pastries, understand the price, pay.

turns.en: Good morning! What can I get you?
Good morning! Two bread rolls, please.
Sure. Anything else?
What is that there, please?

turns.de: Das ist ein Mohnkipferl. Sehr gut zum Frühstück.
turns.en: That's a poppy-seed croissant. Very good for breakfast.
Then I'll take a poppy-seed croissant.
Do you need a bag?
No, thanks. I have one.
That's €2.40.
By card, please.
Thanks. Have a nice day!
Thanks, same to you!

notes: Kipferl is the Austrian word for a crescent-shaped pastry. Semmel = bread roll.
Pointing and saying Das da, bitte (That one, please) always works.

conversations.title: Ordering in a Viennese café
conversations.setting: A traditional Viennese coffee house. You have chosen a table yourself.
conversations.goal: Order a drink and a cake, then pay and tip.

turns.en: Hello, what can I get you?
A Melange, please.
Sure. Anything else?
Do you have apple strudel?

turns.de: Ja, natürlich. Mit oder ohne Schlagobers?
turns.en: Yes, of course. With or without whipped cream?
With whipped cream, please.
Coming right up.
The bill, please!
That's €9.80.
Ten fifty, please. Keep the change.
Thank you! Have a nice day.
Thanks, same to you!

key_phrases.en: Ten fifty, please. Keep the change.

notes: Tipping: say the total you want to pay, including the tip (about 5 to 10 %).
In a Kaffeehaus nobody rushes you. You call the waiter when you want to pay.

conversations.title: Asking the way to the U-Bahn
conversations.goal: Ask, understand the key words, check, thank.

turns.de: Entschuldigung, wie komme ich zur U4?
turns.en: Excuse me, how do I get to the U4?

turns.de: Zur U4? Gehen Sie hier geradeaus und dann links.
turns.en: To the U4? Go straight on here and then left.

turns.de: Geradeaus und dann links. Ist das weit?
turns.en: Straight on and then left. Is it far?

turns.de: Nein, nur drei Minuten zu Fuß.
turns.en: No, only three minutes on foot.

turns.de: Und welche Richtung muss ich nehmen, nach Hütteldorf?
turns.en: And which direction do I take, to Hütteldorf?

turns.de: Das kommt darauf an. Wohin wollen Sie?
turns.en: That depends. Where do you want to go?
To Schönbrunn.
Then towards Hütteldorf, yes.
Thank you very much!
You're welcome!

key_phrases.en: How do I get to the U4?

notes: Repeating the key words back (Geradeaus und dann links?) is a natural way to check you understood.
Vienna U-Bahn lines are named by their end stations: U4 Richtung Hütteldorf or Richtung Heiligenstadt.

conversations.title: Help at the ticket machine
conversations.setting: A Wiener Linien ticket machine in an U-Bahn station.
conversations.goal: Ask for help, understand the answer, say thank you.

turns.de: Entschuldigung, können Sie mir kurz helfen?
turns.en: Excuse me, could you help me for a moment?
Yes, of course. What do you need?

turns.de: Ich möchte eine Fahrkarte für eine Fahrt.
turns.en: I'd like a ticket for one journey.
Press 'single ticket' here.
Do I have to validate the ticket?

turns.de: Ja, bei den blauen Kästen vor der Rolltreppe. Oder Sie kaufen das Ticket in der App.
turns.en: Yes, at the blue boxes before the escalator. Or you buy the ticket in the app.

turns.de: Ah, verstehe. Gilt das Ticket auch für die Straßenbahn?
turns.en: Ah, I see. Is the ticket also valid for the tram?

turns.de: Ja, in ganz Wien. Sie können auch umsteigen.
turns.en: Yes, all over Vienna. You can change too.

turns.de: Super, vielen Dank für die Hilfe!
turns.en: Great, thanks a lot for the help!
You're welcome. Have a good trip!

key_phrases.en: Could you help me for a moment?
Is the ticket also valid for ...?

notes: Paper tickets bought at a machine must be validated (entwerten) before the trip. App tickets don't need it.
If you study in Vienna, ask about the semester ticket: Semesterticket.

conversations.title: Weather chat at the tram stop
conversations.setting: A cold morning at the tram stop.
conversations.goal: Do the classic Austrian weather small talk.

turns.en: Cold today, isn't it?

turns.de: Ja, sehr kalt! Bei mir zu Hause ist es jetzt viel wärmer.
turns.en: Yes, very cold! Back home it's much warmer now.

turns.de: Das glaub ich. Gestern war's noch so schön.
turns.en: I believe that. Yesterday it was still so nice.

turns.de: Ja. Wie wird das Wetter morgen?
turns.en: Yes. What will the weather be like tomorrow?
I think it'll rain tomorrow.

turns.de: Oje. Dann nehme ich einen Schirm mit.
turns.en: Oh no. Then I'll take an umbrella.

turns.de: Gute Idee. Ah, da kommt die Bim.
turns.en: Good idea. Ah, here comes the tram.
Finally! Have a nice day!

key_phrases.en: What will the weather be like tomorrow?

notes: gell? (or gö?) is the Austrian tag for isn't it? / right?. Recognise it; you can answer with Ja!
Spoken Austrian often shortens: glaub = glaube, war's = war es, regnet's = regnet es.

conversations.title: Finding a time to meet
conversations.goal: Suggest a day and time, react, agree.

turns.de: Wollen wir zusammen für die Prüfung lernen?
turns.en: Shall we study for the exam together?

turns.de: Ja, gute Idee! Wann hast du Zeit?
turns.en: Yes, good idea! When are you free?
On Wednesday afternoon?

turns.de: Am Mittwoch habe ich bis drei Uhr Vorlesung. Geht es um vier?
turns.en: On Wednesday I have lectures until three. Is four okay?

turns.de: Um vier passt. Wo treffen wir uns?
turns.en: Four works. Where shall we meet?

turns.de: In der Bibliothek, im ersten Stock?
turns.en: In the library, on the first floor?

turns.de: Okay. Wie lange haben wir Zeit?
turns.en: Okay. How long do we have?

turns.de: Ich kann bis sieben. Dann fange ich mit der Arbeit an.
turns.en: I can stay until seven. Then I start work.
Perfect. See you Wednesday!
See you Wednesday!

notes: um + clock time, am + day: am Mittwoch um vier.
In Austria the ground floor is the Erdgeschoss; the first floor (erster Stock) is one floor up.

conversations.title: At the pharmacy
conversations.setting: You have a cold and a sore throat.
conversations.goal: Describe a simple health problem and understand the advice.

turns.de: Grüß Gott, was kann ich für Sie tun?
turns.en: Hello, what can I do for you?

turns.de: Ich bin erkältet und ich habe Halsschmerzen.
turns.en: I have a cold and a sore throat.

turns.de: Seit wann haben Sie die Halsschmerzen?
turns.en: Since when have you had the sore throat?
For two days.
Do you have a fever too?
No, no fever.

turns.de: Dann empfehle ich diese Lutschtabletten. Dreimal am Tag.
turns.en: Then I recommend these lozenges. Three times a day.

turns.de: Dreimal am Tag. Was kostet das?
turns.en: Three times a day. How much is it?
€8.90. Get well soon!
Thank you!

notes: seit + time = for/since: seit zwei Tagen, seit Montag. German uses the present tense here.

conversations.title: Reporting a broken heater
conversations.setting: Phone call to the office of your Studentenheim.
conversations.goal: Report a problem and agree a time.

turns.en: Student residence, hello?

turns.de: Guten Tag, hier ist Danish aus Zimmer 312.
turns.en: Hello, this is Danish from room 312.
Yes, what's up?

turns.de: Die Heizung in meinem Zimmer funktioniert nicht.
turns.en: The heating in my room isn't working.
Since when?

turns.de: Seit gestern Abend. Es ist sehr kalt.
turns.en: Since last night. It's very cold.

turns.de: Okay. Der Techniker kann morgen um neun kommen. Passt das?
turns.en: Okay. The technician can come tomorrow at nine. Does that work?

turns.de: Um neun habe ich Vorlesung. Geht es auch am Nachmittag?
turns.en: At nine I have a lecture. Is the afternoon possible too?
Yes, at two.
That works, thanks! Goodbye (on the phone)!

notes: On the phone say Auf Wiederhören (literally: until we hear again).
Passt das? / Passt! is the everyday Austrian way to agree on a time.

conversations.title: At the barber
conversations.goal: Say what you want and handle the small talk.

turns.en: Hi! What are we doing today?

turns.de: Bitte kurz an den Seiten und oben nur ein bisschen kürzer.
turns.en: Short on the sides, please, and just a little shorter on top.

turns.de: Mit der Maschine an den Seiten?
turns.en: With the clippers on the sides?
Yes, number three, please.
Okay. And the beard as well?
Just a little, please.

turns.de: Und, was machst du so? Studierst du?
turns.en: So, what do you do? Are you a student?

turns.de: Ja, an der Uni. Und ich lerne Deutsch.
turns.en: Yes, at the university. And I'm learning German.

turns.de: Na, das klappt ja schon gut! So, schau mal. Passt das?
turns.en: Well, that's already going well! There, have a look. Is that okay?

turns.de: Ja, super, danke! Was kostet das?
turns.en: Yes, great, thanks! How much is it?

notes: Many barbers say du and Servus to young customers. You can answer with du as well.

conversations.title: Family photos
conversations.setting: Sophie sees a photo on your phone.
conversations.goal: Talk about your family with simple sentences.

turns.en: Is that your family?

turns.de: Ja, das sind meine Eltern und meine Geschwister.
turns.en: Yes, those are my parents and my siblings.
How many siblings do you have?

turns.de: Ich habe zwei Brüder und eine Schwester.
turns.en: I have two brothers and a sister.
And who is this here?

turns.de: Das ist meine Schwester. Sie ist Ärztin.
turns.en: That's my sister. She's a doctor.
Wow! And your brother?

turns.de: Mein Bruder studiert noch. Er ist erst zwanzig.
turns.en: My brother is still studying. He's only twenty.
Do you miss your family?

turns.de: Ja, manchmal. Aber wir telefonieren jeden Sonntag.
turns.en: Yes, sometimes. But we talk on the phone every Sunday.

key_phrases.de: Ich habe zwei Brüder und eine Schwester.
key_phrases.en: I have two brothers and a sister.
We talk on the phone every Sunday.

notes: Change the numbers and people to fit your real family. Practise it until it's automatic: family is one of the first small-talk topics.

conversations.title: What did you do yesterday?
conversations.goal: Describe yesterday in three or four Perfekt sentences.

turns.en: What did you do yesterday?
In the morning I studied.
And in the afternoon?

turns.de: Am Nachmittag habe ich eingekauft und gekocht.
turns.en: In the afternoon I went shopping and cooked.
What did you cook?

turns.de: Reis mit Gemüse. Es hat sehr gut geschmeckt!
turns.en: Rice with vegetables. It tasted very good!

turns.de: Klingt gut. Hast du am Abend etwas gemacht?
turns.en: Sounds good. Did you do anything in the evening?

turns.de: Ich habe einen Film gesehen und dann habe ich geschlafen.
turns.en: I watched a film and then I slept.
A quiet day, then.
Exactly. And you?

notes: Most verbs use haben in the Perfekt. Only movement (gehen, fahren) and change (aufstehen) use sein.
